resolved_conflicts.explanation: The registry and firelookout.com say 35 feet. Willhite says the 1935 panoramas, taken from the catwalk, say 40 feet, but he thinks 35 feet is more likely. The record uses 10.7 m (35 feet).

The registry and Washington Lookouts say removed in 1956; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1956; Willhite says removed or destroyed in 1956, and also suggests the poles probably stood until 10 to 20 years ago, which does not fit a 1956 end date well.

notes_for_editor: The WebSearch budget for this run was used up before the search step, so the story rests on the four cited pages only. The public access level is inferred from National Forest ownership and the absence of any permit or gate in the trip report, not from a closure notice; the editor may want to check it. The AWS station name Yoke 8-7 comes from Washington Lookouts only. The Mount Baker-Snoqualmie name (registry) and Mt. Baker National Forest name (Washington Lookouts, Willhite) both appear. No photos were added; the registry's National Archives credits were not checked.
